types.name: ReceiptOutcome
types.doc: Outcome vocabulary. observed/accepted are non-terminal; applied/rejected are terminal.

values.doc: A peer/process observed the causation request.
A peer/process accepted or queued the request.
The requested effect/state change was applied.
The requested effect/state change was rejected.

types.name: CausalReceipt
types.doc: One receipt event for a command/effect causation id.

fields.name: receipt_id
fields.doc: Idempotency key for this receipt event.

fields.name: causation_id
fields.doc: Stable id of the command, event, or effect request this receipt observes.

fields.name: observer
fields.doc: Peer, process, or subsystem that produced the receipt.

fields.name: generation
fields.doc: Producer/editor generation. Consumers discard receipts outside the current generation for the causation id.

fields.name: outcome
fields.doc: Receipt outcome.

fields.name: reason
fields.doc: Optional human/debug rejection reason.

fields.name: payload_hash
fields.doc: Optional hash of the state/payload observed by the receipt.

types.name: CausalReceipts
types.doc: Wire body for the externally-tagged `CausalReceipts` envelope.

fields.name: receipts
fields.doc: Receipt batch.

types.name: DeltaOp
types.doc: One incremental graph mutation. Externally tagged: a single-key object whose key is the PascalCase variant name.

variants.doc: A source cell was changed to `payload`.
A lazily recomputed slot published a concrete value.
A node was dirtied without publishing a concrete value.

Op-log delta form for a QueueCell node: append `payload` to the tail. The op-log delta is the incremental counterpart to the storage-snapshot form (cell-model.md § Wire and snapshot shape); a run of same-direction QueuePush ops fuses into one multi-epoch batch Delta (protocol.md § Backpressure & outbox coalescing).

Op-log delta form for a QueueCell node: remove the head. Carries no value (the popped element is determined by ordered replay); a re-delivered pop is Ignored by the epoch gap rule. Crosses the wire only when consumption is authoritatively replicated (mirror sync); in the default producer→consumer sync the remote consumer's pops are local. A QueuePop/QueueClose is a fusion boundary (order-sensitive).
Op-log delta form for a QueueCell node: mark closed (idempotent, terminal — Closed is distinct from Empty). A fusion boundary.

types.name: CellSetBody
types.doc: Body of a `CellSet` or `QueuePush` op: the node and its new value or appended element.

fields.name: node
fields.doc: Target node.

fields.name: payload
fields.doc: Value, inline or by blob descriptor.

types.name: SlotValueBody
types.doc: Body of a `SlotValue` op: the slot and the value it published.

fields.name: node
fields.doc: Target node.

fields.name: payload
fields.doc: Value, inline or by blob descriptor.

types.name: NodeBody
types.doc: Body of an op that names only its node (`Invalidate`, `NodeRemove`, `QueuePop`, `QueueClose`).

fields.name: node
fields.doc: Target node.

types.name: NodeAddBody
types.doc: Body of a `NodeAdd` op: the new node, its type tag and its initial state.

fields.name: node
fields.doc: New node.

fields.name: type_tag
fields.doc: Binding-defined type tag of the new node.

fields.name: state
fields.doc: Initial node body.

fields.name: key
fields.doc: Optional wire-stable keyed address. A conforming ENCODER omits it when absent; an explicit null is also wire-valid and a decoder MUST read both forms as absent (protocol.md § NodeKey, #lzkeynullstrict). This carried a bare NodeKey $ref until that audit, which made a frame the spec now requires decoders to accept schema-invalid.

types.name: EdgeBody
types.doc: Body of an `EdgeAdd` or `EdgeRemove` op: one dependency edge.

fields.name: dependent
fields.doc: Node that reads `dependency`.

fields.name: dependency
fields.doc: Node read by `dependent`.

types.name: Delta
types.doc: Incremental change set: ordered ops that take the receiver from `base_epoch` to `epoch`.

fields.name: base_epoch
fields.doc: Epoch this delta applies to (must equal the receiver's last_epoch).

fields.name: epoch
fields.doc: New epoch, >= base_epoch + 1. Usually base_epoch + 1; a multi-epoch-span delta has epoch > base_epoch + 1 (epoch - base_epoch = accepted-event span). See protocol.md § Multi-epoch-span delta.

fields.name: ops
fields.doc: Ordered operations.

types.name: NodeId
types.doc: Wire-stable node identifier (u64). The full u64 range is wire-valid; the 2^53-1 bound is a PRODUCER obligation on peers whose runtime represents integers as IEEE-754 doubles, and a decoder that cannot represent a received value exactly MUST reject the frame rather than round it (protocol.md § NodeId / PeerId, #lzspecdecoderbound). Schema validity is therefore u64-wide — a narrower binding refuses at decode, not here.

types.name: IpcValue
types.doc: Externally-tagged delta payload: inline bytes or a shared-memory blob reference.

variants.doc: Inline serialized bytes as JSON array of u8 (NOT base64).
Value stored in a blob backend, by descriptor.

types.name: NodeState
types.doc: Externally-tagged node body: concrete bytes, a shared-memory value, or an opaque (visible but non-serializable) node.

variants.doc: Serialized value bytes as JSON array of u8 (NOT base64).
Value stored in a blob backend, by descriptor.
Visible but non-serializable node: no body crosses the wire.

types.name: NodeKey
types.doc: Optional wire-stable keyed address: a '/'-joined path (e.g. 'scores/alice'). The pattern rejects empty/leading/trailing/double slashes; construction-time code also enforces the ≤1024 *byte* and ≤32 *segment* bounds (see protocol.md § NodeKey). Serialized as a bare string; the field is omitted in self-describing codecs when absent.

types.name: BlobBackendKind
types.doc: Which pluggable backend holds the blob. Optional; defaults to 'shm' (POSIX shared memory) for backward compatibility. The receiver routes resolution by this discriminator.

types.name: ShmBlobRef
types.doc: Descriptor into a blob backend (zero-copy transport). The standard fields locate and integrity-check a byte range within the backend's resolved buffer; `backend` selects which pluggable backend resolves it ('shm' = POSIX shared memory, the default for backward compatibility; 'arrow' = Apache Arrow IPC/Flight; 'in_process' = an in-process arena). See protocol.md § Zero-copy transport. `backend` is optional and defaults to 'shm' so legacy descriptors validate unchanged.

fields.name: offset
fields.doc: Offset of the blob header from the start of the backend's buffer.

fields.name: len
fields.doc: Payload length in bytes, excluding the blob header.

fields.name: generation
fields.doc: Per-write generation, used to reject a stale descriptor after wraparound.

fields.name: epoch
fields.doc: IPC epoch of the message that published this blob.

fields.name: checksum
fields.doc: Non-cryptographic payload checksum for torn-write and stale-region checks.

fields.name: backend
fields.doc: Which pluggable backend holds the blob. Optional; defaults to 'shm' (POSIX shared memory) for backward compatibility. The receiver routes resolution by this discriminator.
